post.description: To price one OCI SKU by its part number (from `records_list`, `search` or Oracle's price list page).

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of the price slice, e.g. `USD`, `EUR`, `JPY` (case-insensitive; default `USD`). Oracle published 50 currencies on 2026-10-17; a code it does not publish fails with `not_found`. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{3}$.

Provider reference: default "USD".

200.description:
One part's list price tiers by Oracle part number: `GET /products/?partNumber=<part>&currencyCode=<currency>` (about 350 bytes). The API answers an unknown part with 200 and `items: null`, mapped to `not_found`; a known part without a price in the currency is also `not_found`. Records are shaped like `records_list`. Collection contract name: `records/get`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Observation time (ms since epoch) stamped by the SDK. |
| `part_number` | string |  |
| `publication_id` | string | Top-level `lastUpdated` of the price list, e.g. `2026-10-08T14:38:16.165Z`: the publication version and the date the prices took effect. |
| `record_count` | number |  |
| `records` | object[] | One record per part x currency x price tier, in the publisher's order. |
| `retrieved_at` | string | UTC time of the fetch (RFC 3339, seconds). |
| `source_url` | string | The API URL fetched. |

post.description: To collect the whole OCI price panel for one currency page by page. Use `records_get` for one part.

continuation.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page. It carries the currency; `currency` may be omitted or must match.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of the price slice, e.g. `USD`, `EUR`, `JPY` (case-insensitive; default `USD`). Oracle published 50 currencies on 2026-10-17; a code it does not publish fails with `not_found`. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{3}$.

Provider reference: default "USD".

page_size.description:
Parts per page (1 to 250, default 100). Most parts have one tier; 54 USD parts have two to four.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 250; default 100.

200.description:
Full current OCI price list in one currency, one record per part x price tier, paged in memory: every page re-fetches `GET /products/?currencyCode=<currency>` (no server pagination exists; `offset` and `limit` are ignored by the API) and returns the next `page_size` parts. The cursor pins the currency, `lastUpdated` and the SHA-256 of the canonical items; a page that finds either changed fails with `invalid_input` code `publication_changed` instead of mixing versions. Segment key: `currency`. Collection contract name: `records/list`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | string | `currencyCodeLocalizations[].currencyCode`, ISO 4217. |
| `derived_fields` | string[] | Fields of this record derived by the program rather than published: `region`, `term_type`, `shape`. |
| `description` | string | `description` as published (48 of 668 parts on 2026-10-08); null when the part has none. |
| `display_name` | string | `displayName`, the SKU description as published (commit terms and shapes live here). |
| `effective_at` | string | Top-level `lastUpdated` of the price list, the date the prices took effect, e.g. `2026-10-08T14:38:16.165Z`. |
| `memory_gb` | object | Always null: not structured in the source. |
| `metric_name` | string | `metricName`, the billing unit, e.g. `OCPU Per Hour`, `Gigabyte (GB) Storage Capacity Per Month`. |
| `operating_system` | object | Always null: not structured in the source. |
| `part_number` | string | `partNumber`, Oracle's SKU id, e.g. `B107951`. |
| `price_model` | string | `prices[].model`; only `PAY_AS_YOU_GO` was seen on 2026-10-08. |
| `publication_id` | string | Top-level `lastUpdated` of the price list (the publication version). |
| `range_max` | number | `prices[].rangeMax`, the tier's upper usage bound (`999999999999999` is open-ended); null for an untiered price. |
| `range_min` | number | `prices[].rangeMin`, the tier's lower usage bound; null for an untiered price. |
| `region` | string | Derived: always `global`. The data has no region; Oracle states "Pay the same price in every region" (oracle.com/cloud/pricing). |
| `retrieved_at` | string | UTC time of the fetch (RFC 3339, seconds). |
| `service_category` | string | `serviceCategory`, the product family, e.g. `Compute - Virtual Machine`. |
| `shape` | string | Derived: the first OCI shape token (`BM.` or `VM.` prefix) in `display_name`, e.g. `BM.Standard.E5.48`; null when the name has none. |
| `source_record_id` | string | `oracle:<partNumber>:<currency>:<tier index>`, e.g. `oracle:B108190:USD:1`. |
| `source_url` | string | `https://apexapps.oracle.com/pls/apex/cetools/api/v1/products/?partNumber=<partNumber>&currencyCode=<currency>`. |
| `tenancy` | object | Always null: not structured in the source. |
| `term_type` | string | Derived from `display_name`: the commitment phrase it states (`Hourly Commit`, `Monthly Commit` or `1 Month Commit`, `1 Year Commit`, `3 Year Commit`, `Resource Commit`); `on_demand` when it states none. |
| `tier_count` | number | Number of tiers the part has in this currency. |
| `tier_index` | number | 0-based position of this tier in the part's `prices[]`. |
| `unit_price` | number | `prices[].value`, the list price per `metric_name` unit in `currency`, copied as published. |
| `vcpu` | object | Always null: not structured in the source. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

post.description: Before a collection to learn the current publication and hash, or to check whether the price list moved since the last snapshot.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of the price slice, e.g. `USD`, `EUR`, `JPY` (case-insensitive; default `USD`). Oracle published 50 currencies on 2026-10-17; a code it does not publish fails with `not_found`. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{3}$.

Provider reference: default "USD".

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Cheap version check of the OCI price list: one `GET /products/?currencyCode=<currency>` (about 200 KB for USD). Returns `lastUpdated` as `publication_id` and `published_at`, the part count, the tier (record) count, the response size and the SHA-256 of the canonical items. Oracle posts no hash of its own and sends an ETag that differs per query and is not honoured by `If-None-Match`, so it is not used. No delta endpoint exists, so `records/changes` is not offered. Collection contract name: `source/status`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content_hash` | string | SHA-256 (hex) of the currency slice's `items` array re-serialised as compact JSON with object keys sorted. Oracle posts no hash. |
| `currency` | string |  |
| `files` | object[] | The publisher URL of the currency slice. No bulk download exists beyond this endpoint. |
| `item_count` | number | Parts in the price list (668 on 2026-10-25). |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Observation time (ms since epoch) stamped by the SDK. |
| `priced_item_count` | number | Parts with a price in `currency`. |
| `publication_id` | string | Top-level `lastUpdated` of the price list, e.g. `2026-10-08T14:38:16.165Z`: the publication version and the date the prices took effect. |
| `published_at` | string | Same as `publication_id` (the contract's published_at). |
| `record_count` | number | Price tiers in `currency`, the number of records a full `records_list` walk returns (727 for USD on 2026-10-25). |
| `retrieved_at` | string | UTC time of the fetch (RFC 3339, seconds). |
| `segment_key` | string | How the collection is segmented: one currency slice per walk. |
| `size_bytes` | number | Decoded response body size in bytes. |
| `source_url` | string | The API URL fetched. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.
